_: What each screen on the Run screen board is FOR, and what good looks like.
Kept apart from the generator (tool/build_screen_board.py) so a diff shows which
descriptions changed rather than which pixels did. Codes are pinned to screens:
never renumber one; a new screen gets a new code, a gone screen is retired.
Per plate: file (the PNG under plates/), name, how (driven = tapped to; built =
opened directly), reach (the taps), job, done (stated so failure is visible),
files (the lib/ files that draw it; --stale reads these), and optionally
isnew (what build 26 or the weeks since 2 Sep changed about it), changed,
note, platform, size. board.previous lists the codes on the last board, so
a plate is flagged new exactly when its code was not on it.
Re-read a plate's job and done whenever `python tool/build_screen_board.py --stale`
names it. No test checks this prose; that command is the only thing that will.

board.title: MGKFitness: Run, every screen at build 29, and 1.0.1 so far
board.eyebrow: apps/mgk_run · build 29 (1.0.0+29) as submitted, with ten plates retaken for 1.0.1
board.lede: Every screen in the running app, rendered from the real widget tree, each with what it is for and what a good version looks like. Use it for the last UI pass before the store screenshots: read the 'done right' line under a plate and check the plate against it.
board.surface: 393×852 iPhone unless marked, with the iPhone's safe areas
changed: 1.0.1 so far, retaken on 3 Oct. The sign-in says which app it is and whose account: Run's icon and name above MGKFitness Account, where it said MGKFitness Profile, drawn by the same piece Lift's sign-in uses, and it is laid out as Lift's: the night-road photograph at full strength above, the choices at the foot with the terms and privacy line under them, and no list of what an account gives (B8, C14, K2, K3). The switch between signing in and making an account is on the email form only, as on Lift, and the icon and name are larger. Signing in now has a row of its own, as on Lift's board: B8, the email form for signing back in (B13, new) and the one for making an account (K3). Delete account calls the login an MGKFitness account too (L1, L2, L3, L7). B1, P1 and C14 show the photograph behind them, which the 1 Oct pictures had been taken too early to load. Only these ten were retaken: every other plate is still the 1 Oct picture, because the fixtures are dated from the day a plate is drawn and a Saturday redraw would have moved plates this release has not touched.

Build 29, from the owner's look at build 28 on TestFlight. The start screen shows where the runner is and what today's session asks for: pace, about how long, effort and how it should feel (R24, R25). 'Add a treadmill run' is a row at the foot of the This week tile, not a button under Start (H1, H2). The coach's line waits for the launch animation, opens out of the mark and is held about five seconds (C1, C6). The map's tiles are drawn at two pixels a point, which no plate can show: a test draws no tiles. Also in 29 and on no plate, because a test has no lock screen: a run's distance, time and pace are shown there while it records, as a Live Activity on the iPhone and a notification on Android.

Build 28, from the first look at build 27 on a phone. The app opens on the icon's mark dashing across and leaving the name RUN behind it (B10 to B12, new). Race week is a week of its own and race day is on the plan (E6, E7, new): until now the Plan tab drew a training run on race day. 'Adjust this week' moved from Home's today card to the Plan tab, under the week (A2, E6). Home's today card offers 'Add a treadmill run' in its place (H1, H2, H3). A run can be deleted, from the bin on Edit run (S8, S9, new). The nav bar's selection is a soft plate behind the tab, which slides when the tab changes: it is on every plate that shows the bar.

Re-drawn on 1 Oct, every plate at one commit, after Lift 2.0.0 was merged in beside Run and the design package both apps share changed under it. Most pictures came out the same as on 30 Sep. The rest are named below, or differ only because the fixtures are dated from today.

Signing in is two steps. Apple, Google and 'Continue with email' come first (B8, C14, K2), and the email form is behind the third (K3, new). On one screen the form's Password and Sign up were below the bottom of a 393pt phone.

The privacy policy says what Apple and Google pass on, names Esri as the map provider, and says map tiles are kept on the phone (T19). The deletion messages give run@mgkfitness.mgkcodes.com in place of the studio's address (L5, L6).

A confirmation floats as a rounded card above the bottom edge instead of a bar across it (T15). The paywall's renewal terms say 'turned off' where they said 'switched off' (Y1 to Y9). The Plan tab before a plan starts has the same lit ground as the tab in week three (P5).

Re-drawn on 30 Sep with the UI fixes for build 27, every plate at one commit. Fixed, with the "done right" line now describing the fixed screen and the old defect kept beside it: G4, G6, G7, H6, P5, T8, K1, T16, F7, S6, C9, G1, R16, R17, R18, R19, R28, R29, R24, T15, C8, P4.

New for build 26: the coach's permission sheet and the notice before any price (C7, C8, C9), reporting a reply (C10 to C12), every paywall answer (Y2 to Y9), the account's subscription states and Manage subscription (T4 to T10), signing out with the erase switch (T11, T12), withdrawing the coach's permission (T13 to T15), every delete-account state (L1 to L7), another account's training on the phone (X1), Precise Location off (R28), finishing and leaving a run (R29, R30), a recovered run (F7, F8), a race too close to plan for (G6, G7) and the Health step (B9).

Also new since 2 Sep: the start screen and count-in (R24, R25), the recentre control and full-screen map (R26, R27), the locked coach line (C6), the week a plan is built (H6, P5), backup and permissions (T16, T17), the legal documents (T18, T19) and the backup prompt (K1, K2).

Every plate is drawn as an iPhone now. The September board was drawn as Android without saying so, and at the wrong screen height for anything that sizes itself to the screen, so sheets were shorter than on a phone.
Three September plates were the wrong picture: B1 was blank, S6 was a copy of S7, and C3/C4 now meet the permission sheet unless the runner has agreed. All three are retaken.
Settings is an index since 11 Sep, so T2 (Settings below the fold) no longer exists. Its code is retired, not reused.

retired.T2: Settings below the fold. Settings fits one screen since 11 Sep; the account, sign-out and deletion moved to T4, T11 and L1.

caveats: A test answers every network image with an error, so maps show their route and position marker on a plain ground. The map provider's credit shows only with tiles, so it is not in any plate: on a phone it reads 'Powered by Esri', sits above the in-run panel, and opens the data sources on a tap.
Settings shows a DEVELOPER block in test and debug builds. The store build ends at Privacy & legal.
Every coach line comes from the offline preview coach. Judge the shape of a conversation, not its words.

Driven plates were reached by tapping through the real app, so the route is proven too. Built plates open the screen directly with the data the app would pass it; the taps are written beside them instead.
Only what a phone or server would answer: the store's reply to a purchase, whether location is on, the deletion endpoint's answer, and where a report goes in C11.

acts.title: The app, whole
acts.sub: Three tabs, with their chrome, for a runner three weeks into a plan
acts.lede: The only plates a runner would recognise at a glance. Everything below is either a state of one of these or a room behind a tap.

acts.title: Arriving
acts.sub: The first launch, walked tap by tap
acts.lede: The app opens on a working tracker and never asks who you are to get there. Every plate here was reached by tapping what a runner taps, so the sequence is proven to join up.

acts.title: Home
acts.sub: Every state of the screen the app opens on
acts.lede: The free app has to read as a whole app, not the paid one with holes in it. These are judged against each other.

bands.title: Without a plan, which is the whole free product
The last run, and where the paid line falls

acts.title: Asking for a plan
acts.sub: What happens after Build a plan
acts.lede: In build 26 a runner reaches this only after an account, the coach's permission, the medical notice and a subscription (act 07). The coach's lines are the offline script, so judge the shape, not the words.

bands.title: A race too close for a block

acts.title: The plan
acts.sub: The week, a week opened, the block and the calendar
acts.lede: A plan starts on the coming Monday, so the week it is built in is its own state. The last band is that week.

bands.title: The week a plan is built

acts.title: Recording a run
acts.sub: The screen a runner actually stares at
acts.lede: Every state of one screen, plus the start screen in front of it. The map has no tiles in a test; its route and position marker are real.

acts.title: After the finish line
acts.sub: The run just recorded, and a run the phone lost
acts.lede: The summary is the payoff of the whole loop. Build 26 adds a second way to arrive at one: a run killed before Finish, recovered at the next launch.

acts.title: The coach
acts.sub: A mark on every screen, and what it takes to open it
acts.lede: Since build 26 every way into the coach goes account, then permission, then the medical notice, then the price. The first band after the mark is that order, walked.

bands.title: The first time: permission, notice, price
The permission on a small phone

acts.title: Paying for the coach
acts.sub: The paywall, and every answer it can give
acts.lede: The purchase has never been completed on a phone, so these are the only look at most of these states before App Review. The prices and tier lines are the stores' copy, supplied by the fixture.

acts.title: Profile
acts.sub: The page about a runner, not about a week
acts.lede: Lifetime totals, records and the year. A record is the fastest stretch found inside a recorded route, which is why a typed-in log has no records.

acts.title: Settings and your account
acts.sub: An index since 11 Sep, and everything behind it
acts.lede: Settings shows what everything is set to; the choices are made one tap in. The subscription states are drawn one by one, because the account is where a runner checks what they are paying for.

bands.title: The account, and where the subscription stands

acts.title: Leaving, and a second account
acts.sub: Deleting the account, and a phone that changes hands
acts.lede: Deleting now erases the phone's copy by default and warns that the subscription keeps renewing; the done screen says exactly what happened to the login.

acts.title: The end of a plan
acts.sub: A block ends on race day, and race day is not a Tuesday
acts.lede: The same Home read five ways depending only on the date of the race, and the week of the race as the Plan tab draws it.

H1.name: Home
H1.reach: Launch › three weeks into a plan
H1.job: The screen the app opens on. It answers what to run today first, then how the week is going, the last run and the longer view.
H1.done: Today's session and Start are readable without scrolling, and the today card has nothing else on it; 'Add a treadmill run' is a full-width row at the foot of This week; a missed session is raised once, with two plain answers (I ran it, Adjust); the coach mark and the nav bar cover nothing you need. If you have to scroll to learn what to run today, it has failed.
H1.note: Drawn on a Thursday. This runner has missed only Tuesday's recovery run, and one easy run that got away is not raised, so the missed-session card is not in this picture. The 30 Sep board, drawn on a Wednesday, showed it.
H1.changed: Build 29: 'Add a treadmill run' was a lone button under Start, on the left with nothing beside it. It is a row on the week tile. Build 28: 'Adjust this week' stood there before it, and moved to the Plan tab (A2).

A2.name: Plan
A2.job: The week the plan set, day by day, with how far away the race is and which week of the block this is.
A2.done: Today's row is the one that stands out; days already gone read as past, not as still to do; the line at the top says the race and the week number; 'Adjust this week' is under the seven days it changes. A runner should never have to work out which week they are in.
A2.changed: Build 28: 'Adjust this week' is here. It was on Home's today card.

A3.name: Profile
A3.job: The runner's own record: lifetime totals, the coach's current reading of their training, records, typical times and the year.
A3.done: Totals are whole numbers a person would say (241 km, 16 h), the coach's line is about this runner rather than a sales line, and the settings gear is the only control in the header.

B1.name: Welcome
B1.job: The first screen anyone sees: what the app is, and the two ways in.
B1.done: Wordmark, promise and Get started are on one screen with nothing to scroll; 'I already have an account' is findable but clearly second. A blank or half-drawn frame here is the whole first impression.
B1.changed: 3 Oct: the photograph behind it is drawn; the 1 Oct picture had been taken before it loaded. The September board's B1 was a blank frame taken before the screen had drawn.

B2.name: The coach says who it is
B2.job: The coach introduces itself and says what the app does, before it asks for anything.
B2.done: Three short lines and one button: no form, no permission, no account. If this screen asks for something it has jumped ahead.

B3.name: What to call you
B3.job: Asks what the coach should call the runner, in the coach's voice.
B3.done: Any name is accepted, and so is none; the field and the send arrow sit where a thumb is. It must not read as the start of a sign-up form.

B4.name: Location, with its reason
B4.job: Asks for location, the one permission the tracker needs, with the reason in the same breath.
B4.done: The reason is in plain words before the phone's own dialog appears, and the button says Continue because the phone's dialog is where the choice is made. On iPhone that dialog offers no 'Always'.

B5.name: The answer is acknowledged
B5.job: Answers the runner's choice before moving on.
B5.done: Allowed and Not now both get a sentence back; Not now is never a dead end and never a nag to try again.

B9.name: Health, for steps only
B9.job: Asks for Apple Health for one thing: step counts on runs recorded here, so each run shows steps and cadence.
B9.done: The sentence promises steps and cadence and nothing else: no workouts imported, no watch runs, nothing written to Health. On Android this step does not exist, and the intro goes straight from location to Home.
B9.isnew: New wording in build 26; it used to promise runs from a watch.

B7.name: Where it lets go
B7.job: The end of the intro: a working run tracker with nothing signed in.
B7.done: Dashes rather than zeros, a way to record straight away, the coach mark present, and no account or plan demanded. If this lands on a sign-in form, the free app has a wall again.

B8.name: Signing back in
B8.reach: B1 › I already have an account
B8.job: Signing back into an existing account.
B8.done: Run's icon and name first, then MGKFitness Account and 'Sign in or create your account': which app this is, and that the login is the suite's. Continue with Apple, Continue with Google and Continue with email, at equal width; under them the Hide My Email line and the terms and privacy line, and nothing else, as on Lift. Email, password and 'Forgot your password?' are behind the third button (B13). Someone who has been here before is not walked through the intro again.
B8.changed: 1.0.1: the sign-in/sign-up switch is on the email form only, as on Lift, and the icon and name are drawn larger. 1.0.1: laid out as Lift's sign-in, the night-road photograph at full strength above and the choices at the foot, with the terms and privacy line under them; the list of what an account gives is gone. 1.0.1: Run's icon and name above MGKFitness Account, where it said MGKFitness Profile; Lift's sign-in draws the same head with its own icon. Build 27: Apple and Google lead, the email form is a second step, and 'Forgot your password?' is new.

B13.name: Signing back in with email
B13.job: Signing back in with an email address, for a runner whose account was made with one.
B13.done: Under Run's icon and MGKFitness Account and 'Welcome back', email, password, Sign in and 'Forgot your password?', then 'New here? Create an account' and 'Other ways to sign in', with the terms and privacy line at the foot: Lift's S3, line for line. A wrong password never says which half was wrong.
B13.isnew: New in 1.0.1, beside K3, so the three sign-in screens sit in a row as Lift's do.

H2.name: Home, no plan
H2.job: Home for a runner who just records: the week's runs and distance, answered from the log.
H2.done: It reads as a complete app, not the paid one with holes in it: the tiles count runs and distance rather than sessions against a plan, 'Add a treadmill run' is a row at the foot of This week, and the coach mark is still there.

H3.name: Before the first run
H3.job: Home before anything has been recorded.
H3.done: Every figure is a dash, never 0.0 km, and the one action is Record a run.

H4.name: The last run, with a coach
H4.job: The last run, read against the session it was meant to answer.
H4.done: 'Asked' sits above 'Ran' with distance and pace for each, so the verdict reads as an answer to the plan rather than a grade. The runner's own numbers are never hidden.

H5.name: The last run, without one
H5.reach: Home › scroll to Last run, not subscribed
H5.job: The same card for a runner whose plan outlived their subscription.
H5.done: Distance, pace and time stay visible; only the reading against the plan is held back, and 'See what a coach adds' opens the gate sheet. An offer with nothing to tap is the failure.

G1.name: The notice
G1.reach: Plan › Build a plan, if the notice was never seen
G1.job: The medical notice, as the plan flow shows it when a runner has not already accepted it.
G1.done: The notice is readable top to bottom, with 'I understand' and 'Not now' at the foot. Since build 26 the coach's door asks this first (C9), so most runners never see it here twice.
G1.changed: Build 27: 'I understand' is full width and the panel reaches the bottom edge (see C9).

G2.name: What are you training for
G2.reach: Plan › Build a plan › (permission, notice, subscription)
G2.job: The first question of a plan: what shape of training the runner wants.
G2.done: Five choices, each with a one-line gloss, and nothing typed. A runner who only wants to record can say so here without being argued with.

G3.name: The intake conversation
G3.reach: G2 › I have a race coming up › an answer
G3.job: The coach gathers what it needs one question at a time.
G3.done: One question per turn, each reflecting what it just heard. The replies are the offline coach's script, so judge the shape, not the words.

G4.name: What it heard
G4.job: Everything the coach heard, handed back to be corrected before anything is built.
G4.done: Every value is editable in place, the days chosen match what was said, and Build my plan only lights when the form is complete. Every weekday chip shows its letter whole.
G4.changed: Build 27: M and W were drawn with their right edge faded out.

G5.name: The plan it built
G5.job: The plan arrives, with its shape in three numbers.
G5.done: Length, biggest week and longest run in whole numbers, the race and the countdown at the top, and one button to the week. The plan starts on the coming Monday, and the line under the race says so ('starts Monday' and its date) rather than naming a week not yet begun.
G5.changed: Build 27: the line read '112 days · week 1 of 16' before week 1 had begun.

G6.name: A race three weeks out
G6.reach: G3 with a race 21 days away › Review details
G6.job: The confirmation screen for a race too close to build a block for.
G6.done: The test sheet (D18) expects the runner to be told here, before anything is built: 'A plan needs at least 6 weeks before race day. Pick a later race, or build a plan without one.' It is said under the date, with 'Build without a race' below it, and the button reads 'Fix the race date above' and stays dark until the date moves or the race comes out.
G6.isnew: The six-week rule is new in build 26.
G6.changed: Build 27: nothing warned here, and Build my plan was lit.

G7.name: And if the builder refuses one
G7.reach: a build the validator refuses (G6 now stops a too-close race first)
G7.job: What the runner meets when the plan builder refuses a plan: here, the race too close, as the real repository and validator refuse it.
G7.done: The coach says plainly why: 'A plan needs at least 6 weeks before race day. Pick a later race, or build a plan without one.' Change the race goes back to the details as confirmed, and Not now leaves. No validator text anywhere, and no Try again, because the same details would be refused the same way.
G7.changed: Build 27: it showed 'That did not work, and it is on me rather than on you' above the validator's own error text, with a Try again that failed identically. Built rather than driven now, because G6 no longer lets the race through.

P1.name: This week
P1.job: A week of a plan, sessions named as activities, with rest days as rest.
P1.done: Each row says what kind of run and how far in whole kilometres; no time of day is invented; rest days are visibly lighter. Built from a July fixture, so its dates are fixed.
P1.changed: 3 Oct: the photograph behind the week is drawn; the 1 Oct picture had been taken before it loaded.

P2.name: A week opened
P2.job: One week in full, with the target pace for each session.
P2.done: The day the runner tapped stays highlighted; each session has a target pace; a provisional week says so at the top.

P3.name: The whole block
P3.job: The shape of the whole block: phases, volume week by week, and the taper.
P3.done: The curve peaks and then tapers into race day; phases are labelled; totals are whole numbers. It must read as one plan, not a second competing one.

P4.name: Week by week
P4.job: The block as a calendar, opening on the current week.
P4.done: It opens on the week today falls in, its title ('This week' and its dates) at the top under the header, with today highlighted; later weeks say they firm up closer to the time.
P4.changed: Build 27: the title opened tucked under the header, the first card starting mid-way.

N3.name: The tab with no plan
N3.job: Where a plan is offered to someone who has none.
N3.done: Says no plan is fine, offers Build a plan once, and explains how plans work below. Not hidden, not nagging.

H6.name: Home, the week a plan is built
H6.reach: Build a plan on a Wednesday › See my week › Home
H6.job: Home in the days between building a plan and the Monday it starts.
H6.done: Home and the Plan tab agree on when training starts. Today says 'Your plan starts Monday' and its date, what the first session is, and that nothing is set before then, over Record a run; the week is counted from the runner's own runs, not against sessions not yet due. Read it beside P5.
H6.isnew: Plans start on the coming Monday since build 25.
H6.changed: Build 27: Home prescribed '5 km today' off next week's same weekday and counted '0 of 7' for this week.

P5.name: Plan, the week a plan is built
P5.job: The Plan tab on the day a plan is built.
P5.done: The week shown is the one the plan starts with, headed 'Starts Monday' and its date rather than 'This week', and no day of it is lit as today. The header above agrees: the countdown, then 'starts Monday' and the date, not a week number.
P5.changed: Build 27: it was headed 'This week' (next week's dates) with next Wednesday lit as today. The header read '112 days · week 1 of 16'.

R24.name: Before the clock
R24.job: The start screen: where the runner is, whether the GPS is ready, what today's session asks for, and a Start that does not start the clock yet.
R24.done: A dot marks the runner in the middle of the map above the panel. The panel leads with the GPS ('GPS ready', and how close), then the session: distance and name, the pace band, about how long, the effort out of ten, and one line on how it should feel. Start is the only button. Nothing is being timed yet. (The ground is plain: a test draws no map tiles.)
R24.changed: Build 29: it said '6 km · easy run' over a map with nothing on it to say where the runner was. Build 27: it read '6.00 km · easy' where Home says '6 km'.
R24.note: With no time trial there is no pace or time, only effort and feel. With no session the panel says 'Free run'. The dot follows a fix taken every three seconds; a pan parks the map and a recentre control appears.

R25.name: The count-in
R25.job: Three seconds to put the phone away before recording begins.
R25.done: A big count and a Stop that returns to the start screen with nothing recorded. The map and the panel are dimmed almost to black under it, so the numeral is the only thing to read.

R1.name: Acquiring
R1.job: The recording screen before the first GPS fix.
R1.done: Says it is acquiring GPS; figures sit at 0.00 and dashes, not guesses.

R2.name: First few hundred metres
R2.job: The first moments of a planned run.
R2.done: Distance ticks up from the first fix; the session's brief is visible because the pace verdict is still held.

R3.name: Warming up
R3.done: No pace verdict yet (it says 'Finding your pace'), because a rolling pace off a standing start would read as 'you are slow'.

R4.name: Warmed up
R4.done: A verdict (On target here) with the band's edge named; the panel shrinks to give the map back its height.

R5.name: Deep into it
R5.done: The route has a shape worth the space; distance, time, pace and distance to go all readable at arm's length.

R6.name: Paused
R6.job: Pausing, and the only place Finish appears.
R6.done: Resume and Finish replace Lap and Pause; the status says Paused. Finish is never one of three buttons side by side while running.

R7.name: Lap taken
R7.job: A manual lap during a run.
R7.done: Lap stays available while running and changes nothing destructive.

R8.name: Panel raised
R8.job: The panel at its full height, with the session brief and splits.
R8.done: Splits and the brief are readable without clipping. At full height the panel covers the close control and the status line; check that is acceptable while running.

R26.name: Map moved by hand
R26.job: The runner has panned the map away from themselves.
R26.done: A recentre control appears, and only after the map has been moved; the panel does not move with the map.

R27.name: Map full screen
R27.job: The panel at its lowest: distance and time only, the map full screen.
R27.done: Two figures, a handle, nothing clipped; the content swaps rather than being cut off.

R29.name: Finishing
R29.job: The moment between tapping Finish and the summary opening.
R29.done: Both buttons show a spinner and ignore further taps, so a double tap makes one run. Each spinner sits clear of its label, in the label's own grey.
R29.changed: Build 27: the spinners touched their labels, and Resume's was dark on grey.

R30.name: Leaving mid-run asks first
R30.reach: Recording › close, Back, or the iPhone edge swipe
R30.job: Any way out of a live run asks whether to throw it away.
R30.done: 'Discard this run?' with Keep running and a red Discard. Keep running carries on recording. Back must never leave a run recording out of sight.

R9.name: Easy · slower than the band
R9.done: Easy caps effort rather than bounding it, so running slow is On target and the lower edge is not named.

R10.name: Easy · faster than the band
R10.job: An easy session run too fast.
R10.done: The verdict tells the runner to ease off, with the cap named.

R11.name: Threshold · slower
R11.job: A threshold session run too slow.
R11.done: Both edges of the band are named and the verdict says pick it up.

R12.name: Threshold · faster
R12.done: The verdict says ease off; the same band, read the other way.

R13.name: No plan · early
R13.reach: Home › Record a run, no plan
R13.done: No brief, no band, no verdict, and no gap where they would be. It is a complete screen, not a degraded one.

R14.name: No plan · running
R14.done: The numbers are the whole screen, and they read cleanly.

R15.name: Signal lost
R15.job: The GPS has stopped arriving mid-run.
R15.done: The status says No signal, pace shows dashes rather than a stale figure, and the run keeps recording; what is already recorded is safe on the phone.

R16.name: Location refused
R16.job: Location was refused at the start.
R16.done: A plain sentence saying nothing is tracked until it is allowed, with Continue to ask again, and Close as the only control on the row: this run never started, so there is nothing to resume or finish. The panel carries no session either: no effort brief, no "To go", only the zeros that are true.

S8.name: Correcting a run
S8.job: Fixing the numbers on a run already in the log, and the way to delete it.
S8.done: Every field opens holding what was stored. The line at the top says the route does not change. The bin is in the top bar, on screen without scrolling: it was first put under Notes, below the fold, where nobody would have found it.

S9.name: Deleting a run
S9.job: The question asked before a run is deleted.
S9.done: It says what goes (the run and its route, from the phone and the backup) and that it cannot be undone. 'Keep it' is the quiet answer and Delete is red. With no signal and a backup, it refuses and says to check the connection, because a run deleted only on the phone would come back from the backup.
